title: Three climates, one country
standfirst: A long, narrow country with three weather systems running at once, which makes timing the whole trick.

blocks.heading: Two regions, joined by a short flight
paras: North, centre and south are each on their own calendar, and no month is good for all three at once.
We plan two regions and accept that the third waits for another trip. Members who insist on the full length usually spend a third of it in airports.

blocks.heading: The bays, privately
blocks.caption: A private boat rather than a scheduled cruise.
paras: The famous bays are worth the reputation and the scheduled boats are not. Cabins are small, routes are fixed and the anchorages are shared.
A private junk for two nights costs less than people expect, and it goes where the fleet does not.

blocks.heading: Food as the itinerary
blocks.caption: Markets at dawn, which is when they are worth seeing.
paras: Vietnam is one of the few countries where planning the days around eating is a serious strategy rather than an indulgence.
We build mornings around markets and evenings around a handful of tables that need booking weeks ahead.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: North October to April, centre February to May, south December to April. Pick two that overlap.
Ten nights for two regions. Fourteen if a beach is wanted at the end.
Yes, with short flights between regions rather than long drives, and with the food handled rather than left to chance.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
